author: Norman Littleford
poem_text_en:
Rampaging through the heavens
Never stopping day or night,
A spectacle of a lifetime
A comet in full flight.
Faster than a cheetah
With a tail that’s miles long,
Bigger than a mountain
So powerful and strong.
The outer ice is melting
Causing vapor from the force,
And leaves a trail behind it
As it travels on its course.
If one should come too close to earth
The atmosphere will shake,
With shockwave reaching to the ground
Causing the land to quake.
Scientists say the chemicals
In the dust they leave behind,
Could have started life on the earth
Which resulted in mankind.
I cannot say if this is true
I do not have the right,
But I know no better spectacle
Than a comet in full flight.
summary_en: The poem describes a comet's rapid journey through the heavens, emphasizing its immense size, speed, and powerful presence. The poet reflects on scientific theories suggesting comets may have brought the elements that sparked life on Earth. Ultimately, the poet concludes that witnessing a comet in full flight remains the most magnificent spectacle of a lifetime.

figures_of_speech.note_en: The speed of the comet is compared to a cheetah using the word 'than'.
The size of the comet is compared to a mountain to emphasize its magnitude.

rules.rule_en: Norman Littleford (1889–1947) was an American poet.
The comet is described as a 'spectacle of a lifetime'.
